prompt: Solve the inequality $-4x + 3 < 23$. Write your answer like "x > -5".

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler: $-4x < 8$ gives $x > -2$ (sign flips!). Yours just needs the $+3$ moved over first.
Now divide by $-4$. Dividing by a negative FLIPS the sign: $<$ becomes $>$.

explanation: Divide both sides by $-4$ and flip $<$ to $>$: $x > -5$.
Check: $x = 0$ gives $3 < 23$ ✓, and $x = -6$ gives $24 + 3 = 27$, which is not $< 23$ — the boundary is $-5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: On a number line
steps: Put an OPEN dot at $-5$, since $-5$ itself gives $23 < 23$, which is false.
Shade to the right: every number bigger than $-5$ makes the left side smaller than 23.
